questions.q: At $1990K$ and $1atm$ pressure, there are equal number of ${Cl}_{2}$ molecules and $Cl$ atoms in the reaction mixture. The value of ${K}_{p}$ for the reaction ${Cl}_{2\left(g\right)} = 2{Cl}_{\left(g\right)}$ under the above conditions is $x \times {10}^{- 1} .$ The value of $x$ is______(Rounded off to the nearest integer)
questions.solution:
${Cl}_{2} ⇌ 2Cl$

Let mol of both of ${Cl}_{2}$ and $Cl$ is $x$

${P}_{Cl} = \dfrac{x}{2x} \times 1 = \dfrac{1}{2}atm$

${P}_{{Cl}_{2}} = \dfrac{x}{2x} \times 1 = \dfrac{1}{2}atm$

${K}_{p} = \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2}}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2} = 0 . 5 ⇒ 5 \times {10}^{- 1}$

questions.q:
The stepwise formation of ${\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{4}\right]}^{2 +}$ is given below:

${Cu}^{2 +} + {NH}_{3}\overset{{K}_{1}}{⇌}{\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)\right]}^{2 +}$

${\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)\right]}^{2 +} + {NH}_{3}\overset{{K}_{2}}{⇌}{\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{2}\right]}^{2 +}$

${\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{2}\right]}^{2 +} + {NH}_{3}\overset{{K}_{3}}{⇌}{\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{3}\right]}^{2 +}$

${\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{3}\right]}^{2 +} + {NH}_{3}\overset{{K}_{4}}{⇌}{\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{4}\right]}^{2 +}$

The value of stability constants ${K}_{1}, {K}_{2}, {K}_{3}$ and ${K}_{4}$ are ${10}^{4}, 1 . 58 \times {10}^{3}, 5 \times {10}^{2}$ and ${10}^{2}$ respectively. The overall equilibrium constants for dissociation of ${\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{4}\right]}^{2 +}$ is $x \times {10}^{- 12} .$ The value of $x$ is _____ (Rounded off to the nearest integer)
questions.solution:
${Cu}^{2 +} + {NH}_{3}\overset{{K}_{1}}{⇌}{\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)\right]}^{2 +}$

${\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)\right]}^{2 +} + {NH}_{3}\overset{{K}_{2}}{⇌}{\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{2}\right]}^{2 +}$

${\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{2}\right]}^{2 +} + {NH}_{3}\overset{{K}_{3}}{⇌}{\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{3}\right]}^{2 +}$

${\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{3}\right]}^{2 +} + {NH}_{3}\overset{{K}_{4}}{⇌}{\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{4}\right]}^{2 +}$

${Cu}^{2 +} + 4{NH}_{3}\overset{K}{⇌}{\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{4}\right]}^{2 +}$

So,

$K = {K}_{1} \times {K}_{2} \times {K}_{3} \times {K}_{4}$

$= {10}^{4} \times 1 .58 \times {10}^{3} \times 5 \times {10}^{2} \times {10}^{2}$

$K = 7 .9 \times {10}^{11}$

Where $K \to$ Equilibrium constant for formation of ${\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{4}\right]}^{2 +}$
So equilibrium constant $\left({K}^{'}\right)$ for dissociation
$\text{of}{\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{4}\right]}^{2 +}\text{is}\dfrac{1}{K}$

${K}^{'} = \dfrac{1}{K}$

${K}^{'} = \dfrac{1}{7 . 9 \times {10}^{11}}$

$= 1 . 26 \times {10}^{- 12} = \left(x \times {10}^{- 12}\right)$

So the value of $x = 1 . 26$

$OMR$ Ans $= 1$ (After rounded off to the nearest integer)

$logk = logA - \dfrac{Ea}{2 . 303RT}$

$\left|Slope\right| = \dfrac{Ea}{2 . 303R} = 10, 000$

$log\left(\dfrac{{k}_{2}}{{k}_{1}}\right) = \dfrac{Ea}{2 . 303R}\left(\dfrac{1}{{T}_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{{T}_{2}}\right)$

$log\left(\dfrac{{10}^{- 4}}{{10}^{- 5}}\right) = 10, 000\left[\dfrac{1}{500} - \dfrac{1}{{T}_{2}}\right]$

$log\left(\dfrac{{10}^{- 4}}{{10}^{- 5}}\right) = 10, 000\left[\dfrac{1}{500} - \dfrac{1}{{T}_{2}}\right]$

${T}_{2} = 526 . 31 ≃ 526K$

Hence answer is $\left(526\right)$

questions.solution:
${\left(t\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}_{500torr} = 240sec = 4min$

${\left(t\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}_{250torr} = 4min .$

$t\dfrac{1}{2} ∝ {a}^{1 - n}$

$\dfrac{{\left({t}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}\right)}_{1}}{{\left(t\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}_{2}} = {\left(\dfrac{{a}_{1}}{{a}_{2}}\right)}^{1 - n}1 = {2}^{0} = {\left(\dfrac{250}{500}\right)}^{1 - n}n = 1$

As $t\dfrac{1}{2}$ is independent of initial pressure. Hence, order is $1$st order.

Given that reaction is first order with respect to X and of zero order with respect to Y.

Means $r = k\left[X\right]{\left[Y\right]}^{0}$ Where k = rate constant.

Using data from $I$ & $III$

$\dfrac{M \times {10}^{- 3}}{2 \times {10}^{- 3}} = \dfrac{0 . 4}{0 . 1} ⇒ M = 8$

Not the ratio which is asked in question

$\dfrac{M}{L} = \dfrac{8}{0 . 2} = 40$

Experiment $\dfrac{\left[X\right]}{{molL}^{- 1}}$ $\dfrac{\left[Y\right]}{{molL}^{- 1}}$ $\dfrac{Initial rate}{mol{L}^{- 1}{min}^{- 1}}$
I $0 . 1$ $0 . 1$ $2 \times {10}^{- 3}$
II $L$ $0 . 2$ $4 \times {10}^{- 3}$
III $0 . 4$ $0 . 4$ $M \times {10}^{- 3}$
IV $0 . 1$ $0 . 2$ $2 \times {10}^{- 3}$

Examine the data of table and calculate ratio of numerical values of $M$ and $L$.
questions.explanation:
Given that reaction is first order with respect to X and of zero order with respect to Y.

Means $r = k\left[X\right]{\left[Y\right]}^{0}$ Where k = rate constant.

Using data $I$ & $II$

$\dfrac{4 \times {10}^{- 3}}{2 \times {10}^{- 3}} = \left(\dfrac{L}{0 . 1}\right){\left(\dfrac{0 . 2}{0 . 1}\right)}^{0} ⇒ L = 0 . 2$

Using data from $I$ & $III$

$\dfrac{M \times {10}^{- 3}}{2 \times {10}^{- 3}} = \dfrac{0 . 4}{0 . 1} ⇒ M = 8$

Not the ratio which is asked in question

$\dfrac{M}{L} = \dfrac{8}{0 . 2} = 40$

$\dfrac{{t}_{1}}{{t}_{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{k}ln\dfrac{{a}_{0}}{0 . 4{a}_{0}}}{\dfrac{1}{k}ln\dfrac{{a}_{0}}{0 . 1{a}_{0}}}$

$\dfrac{540}{{t}_{2}} = \dfrac{ln\dfrac{10}{4}}{ln10}$

questions.q:
The number of correct statements from the following is ___________

(A) Conductivity always decreases with decrease in concentration for both strong and weak electrolytes.

(B) The number of ions per unit volume that carry current in a solution increases on dilution.

(C) Molar conductivity increases with decrease in concentration.

(D) The variation in molar conductivity is different for strong and weak electrolytes.

(E) For weak electrolytes, the change in molar conductivity with dilution is due to decrease in degree of dissociation.
questions.solution:
Conductivity always decreases with the decrease in concentration both, for weak and strong electrolytes.

This can be explained by the fact that the number of ions per unit volume that carry the current in a solution decreases on dilution.

Molar conductivity of a strong and weak electrolyte increases with dilution. On dilution as volume of solution increases. Thus, on dilution, ions get more apart and mobility of ions increases which leads to increase in molar conductivity of the solution.

Except $\left(B\right)$ and $\left(E\right)$, all statements are correct.

Solubility $= \left(\dfrac{x}{m}\right)$ mole/lit
${A}_{3}{B}_{2}\left(s\right)\mathop{⇌ 3{A}^{2 +}}_{\dfrac{3x}{M}}\mathop{( aqs ) + 2{B}^{3 -} ( aqs )}_{2\left(\dfrac{x}{M}\right)}$
${K}_{sp} = {\left(\dfrac{3x}{M}\right)}^{3}{\left(\dfrac{2x}{M}\right)}^{2}$
$= \left(3\right){}^{3}{\left(2\right)}^{2}{\left(\dfrac{x}{m}\right)}^{5}$
$= 27 \times 4{\left(\dfrac{x}{m}\right)}^{5}$
$= 108{\left(\dfrac{x}{m}\right)}^{5} = a{\left(\dfrac{x}{M}\right)}^{5}$
So $a = 108$

questions.q: At $310K$, the solubility of ${CaF}_{2}$ in water is $2 . 34 \times {10}^{- 3}g / 100mL$. The solubility product of ${CaF}_{2}$ is ---- $\times {10}^{- 8}{\left(mol / L\right)}^{3}$(nearest integer). (Given molar mass : ${CaF}_{2} = 78g{mol}^{- 1}$)
questions.solution:
The solubility product constant is the equilibrium constant for the dissolution of a solid substance into an aqueous solution. It is denoted by the symbol ${K}_{sp}$.

Solubility of ${CaF}_{2} = Smole / / L$

$S = \dfrac{2 . 34 \times {10}^{- 3}}{0 . 1 \times 78} = \dfrac{2 . 34}{78} \times {10}^{- 2} = 3 \times {10}^{- 4}mol / L$

${K}_{sp}\left({CaF}_{2}\right) = 4{S}^{3} = 4{\left(3 \times {10}^{- 4}\right)}^{3}$

$= 108 \times {10}^{- 12}$

$= 0 . 0108 \times {10}^{- 8}{\left(mol / L\right)}^{3}$

questions.q:
When light of wavelength $248nm$ falls on a metal of threshold energy $3 . 0eV$, the de-Broglie wavelength of emitted electrons is ________ $\overset{o}{A}$. (Round off to the Nearest Integer).

[Use : $\sqrt{3} = 1 . 73, h = 6 . 63 \times {10}^{- 34}Js; {m}_{e} = 9 . 1 \times {10}^{- 31}kg; c = 3 . 0 \times {10}^{8}{ms}^{- 1}; 1eV = 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}J ]$
questions.solution:
Energy incident $= \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$

$= \dfrac{6 . 63 \times {10}^{- 34} \times 3 . 0 \times {10}^{8}}{248 \times {10}^{- 9} \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}}eV$

$= \dfrac{6 . 63 \times 3 \times 100}{248 \times 1 . 6}$

$= 0 . 05eV \times 100 = 5eV$

Now using

$E = ϕ + K . E$

$5 = 3 + K . E .$

$K . E . = 2eV = 3 . 2 \times {10}^{- 19}J$

for de Broglie wavelength $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}$

$K . E . = \dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2}$

so $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2K . E .}{m}}$

hence $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2K . E . \times m}}$

$= \dfrac{6 . 63 \times {10}^{- 34}}{\sqrt{2 \times 3 . 2 \times {10}^{- 19} \times 9 . 1 \times {10}^{- 31}}}$

$= \dfrac{6 . 63}{7 . 6} \times \dfrac{{10}^{- 34}}{{10}^{- 25}} = \dfrac{66 . 3 \times {10}^{- 10}m}{7 . 6}$

$= 8 . 72 \times {10}^{- 10}m$

$\approx 9 \times {10}^{- 10}m$

$= 9\overset{o}{A}$

$= - 15347 . 7J$

or, $W = - 15 . 35kJ$

$∴ q = - W$

or, $q = 15 . 35kJ$ (for $5$ moles)

$∴ q / mole = \dfrac{15 . 35}{5} = 3kJ{mol}^{- 1}$

questions.q:
$28 . 0$ L of ${CO}_{2}$ is produced on complete combustion of $16 . 8L$ gaseous mixture of ethene and methane at $25 ° C$ and $1$ atm. Heat evolved during the combustion process is $kJ$

Given$: {\Delta H}_{C}\left({CH}_{4}\right) = - 900kJ{mol}^{- 1}$

${\Delta H}_{C}\left({C}_{2}{H}_{4}\right) = - 1400kJ{mol}^{- 1}$.
questions.solution:
Complete combustion of ethene and methane mixture produces carbon dioxide.
Let, Volume of ${C}_{2}{H}_{4}$ is $x$ litre

${C}_{2}{H}_{4} + 3{O}_{2} \to 2{CO}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O$

Initial volume of carbon dioxide 0
Final volume of carbon dioxide $2x$

${CH}_{4} + 2{O}_{2} \to {CO}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O$

Initial volume of carbon dioxide is 0

Final volume of carbon dioxide is $( 16 . 8 - x )$

Total volume of ${CO}_{2} = 2x + 16 . 8 - x$

$⇒ 28 = 16 . 8 + x$

$x = 11 . 2L$

${n}_{{CH}_{4}} = \dfrac{PV}{RT} = \dfrac{1 \times 5 . 6}{0 . 082 \times 298} = 0 . 229mole$

${n}_{{C}_{2}{H}_{4}} = \dfrac{11 . 2}{0 . 082 \times 298} = 0 . 458mole$

$∴$ Heat evolved using standard enthalpy of combustion $= 0 . 229 \times 900 + 0 . 458 \times 1400$

$= 206 . 1 + 641 . 2$

$= 847 . 3kJ$
